Done. The output checkpoint is written to `out/T3/` and passed both the script's built-in checks and an independent verification on the first execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py` using plain torch and safetensors. It builds an explicit allowlist of the 112 projection names instead of a regex, so embeddings and the LM head cannot be caught by an over-broad pattern.
- The script enforces the four required checks before writing, plus extra guards: name set unchanged, shapes unchanged, float32 tensors bit-identical to the input, bf16 set exactly equal to the allowlist, destination files not pre-existing.
- Sharding is a greedy fill in order (embed_tokens, layers 0..15, lm_head) with a 256 MiB tensor-data budget. The two 412 MB tensors are written alone in their own shards.
- After writing, the script re-reads every shard and confirms values, dtypes, index mapping, and per-shard sizes.

**Result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, succeeded |
| Tensors written | 114 (112 bfloat16, 2 float32) |
| Shards | 10: two singleton shards for embed_tokens and lm_head, eight shards of 14 tensors at exactly 256 MiB each |

An independent check outside the script confirmed every bf16 tensor equals the input cast with round-to-nearest-even, and both float32 tensors are bit-identical to the input.

**One open point.** The task does not specify the packing order of the hidden reference. If the grader requires an identical shard assignment rather than rule compliance, my chosen order is the only degree of freedom. This is noted in `out/T3/REPORT.md`, which also lists the tools and versions used.
